vocabulary.definition: a task or project that is difficult or takes time to complete
vocabulary.example: The construction of the new bridge was a massive undertaking that required skilled engineers and laborers.

vocabulary.definition: to travel all the way around something, especially the world
vocabulary.example: Ferdinand Magellan was the first explorer to circumnavigate the globe.

vocabulary.definition: a lack of proportion or relation between corresponding things
vocabulary.example: The imbalance in trade between the two countries led to disputes over tariffs.

vocabulary.definition: to forcefully remove something or someone from a location or position
vocabulary.example: The firefighters worked hard to dislodge the trapped hiker from the narrow crevice.

vocabulary.definition: a spreading, pervasive, and usually unintentional effect or influence
vocabulary.example: The closure of the factory had a ripple effect on the entire community, leading to job losses in various sectors.

vocabulary.definition: individuals who examine and evaluate information to provide insights and recommendations
vocabulary.example: Financial analysts predicted a rise in stock prices based on the company's quarterly earnings report.
